introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0550 Geography 1, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board). Time allowed: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions in this examination. Calculators are allowed; mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate and mark only one answer for each question: if more than one answer is marked, the question scores zero. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; if a question is difficult, move on and come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Question 3 refers to a figure of four settlement patterns.

questions.enonce_markdown: An expression of the relationship between measurements on the map and those actually done on the ground is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **scale** of a map is the ratio between a distance measured on the map and the corresponding distance on the ground (for example 1:50,000 means that 1 cm on the map stands for 50,000 cm on the ground). Distance and area are simply measurements, and the key (legend) only explains the symbols used on the map.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If the distance between Bamenda and Buea on a map is 500 cm. What would be the actual distance if the map has a scale of 1:50,000?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A scale of 1:50,000 means that 1 cm on the map represents 50,000 cm on the ground.

Ground distance = map distance $\times$ scale denominator = $500 \times 50\,000 = 25\,000\,000$ cm.

Convert to metres: $25\,000\,000 \div 100 = 250\,000$ m.

Convert to kilometres: $250\,000 \div 1\,000 = 250$ km.

The common mistake is to forget one of the two conversions (cm to m, then m to km), which gives 250 m or 500 km.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The settlement patterns shown on the figure labelled A, B, C, D are respectively:

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Read the pattern of houses in each part of the figure:

- **A**: the houses are strung out along one road, one behind the other, so the pattern is **linear**.
- **B**: only a few houses, far apart and scattered with no clear grouping, so the pattern is **dispersed**.
- **C**: many houses packed closely together around a road junction, in an irregular cluster, so the pattern is **nucleated**.
- **D**: houses lined up in regular rows along roads that cross at right angles, showing a deliberate layout, so the pattern is **planned**.

The order Linear, Dispersed, Nucleated, Planned matches option D.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An evidence on the map that indicates a tourist function is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A tourist function is shown by facilities that serve visitors and leisure, such as hotels, a golf course, a camp site or a viewpoint. A church and a post office are ordinary services for the local population, and a built-up area only shows where people live. A **golf course** is a recreation facility, so it is the evidence of a tourist function.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Features on an Ordnance Map Extract are located using:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A feature on a topographic (Ordnance) map is located with a **grid reference**: the numbers of the vertical lines (eastings) are given first, then the numbers of the horizontal lines (northings). Bench marks show heights, cardinal points give directions and conventional signs are the symbols that show what a feature is, not where it is.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Some places on the earth surface have four seasons while others have just two. This is due to the movement of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Seasons result from the **revolution of the earth round the sun** together with the tilt of the earth's axis (about 23.5 degrees). Because of this, the amount of heat received changes during the year, strongly in the middle latitudes (four seasons) and little near the equator, where the seasons are reduced to rainy and dry. The sun does not move round the earth, and winds and ocean water do not cause the seasons.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the Latitudes below will experience the shortest length of day during Summer solstice on June 21st
questions.corrige_markdown:
On June 21 the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the sun. Places in the north have long days: 66½°N has a very long day and 90°N (the North Pole) has 24 hours of daylight. In the southern hemisphere the days are short. The circle at 66½°S (the Antarctic Circle) is just at the limit where the sun hardly rises, and at **90°S (the South Pole) the sun stays below the horizon for the whole day**, so its length of day is zero. Hence 90°S has the shortest day.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The earth is divided into two equal halves by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **great circle** is a circle on the surface of the earth whose plane passes through the centre of the earth, so it divides the earth into two equal halves (hemispheres). The equator and any pair of opposite meridians (for example the Prime Meridian with the 180th meridian) are great circles. Other lines of latitude are small circles, and time zones are strips of the earth's surface, not circles dividing it into halves.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An area of land drained by a main river and its tributaries is the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **drainage basin** (river basin) is the whole area of land drained by a main river and all its tributaries. The watershed is the high ground (the divide) that separates one drainage basin from another, while the hydrological cycle and the water cycle are the same thing: the circulation of water between the sea, the atmosphere and the land.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The process by which water soaks from the surface into the soil is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Infiltration** is the entry of water from the surface into the soil. Percolation is the later downward movement of water through the soil and rock, throughflow is the sideways flow of water in the soil towards a river, and base flow is the groundwater that feeds a river between rains.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Part of the rain gauge is sunk into the ground so as to prevent:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a standard rain gauge the collecting bottle (glass jar) is placed in the ground so that it stays cool and steady: it is **shielded from the sun's heat, which would otherwise evaporate the rain already collected** and give a reading that is too low. Splashing is prevented by a different feature, the funnel rim, which stands above the ground (about 30 cm). The gauge is set in an open place away from trees and buildings, which prevents run-off from them. Groundwater cannot enter a jar sealed under a funnel.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: rain from splashing from the ground into the funnel.
run off from trees and buildings from entering the funnel.
sun's heat from evaporating any rain collected in the glass jar.

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of a planetary wind is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Planetary (permanent) winds blow all year round in the same general direction, from the subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low-pressure belt: they are the **trade winds** (north-east and south-east trades), together with the westerlies and the polar easterlies. Mountain and katabatic winds are local winds, and monsoon winds are seasonal winds that reverse direction during the year.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A climatic region that has two rainy seasons and two dry seasons is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The sun is overhead the equator twice a year (at the equinoxes), which brings two periods of heavy rain separated by two shorter drier periods. This is the pattern of the **equatorial climate** (for example in southern Cameroon). Monsoon climates have one wet and one dry season, continental climates have a strong contrast between summer and winter, and deserts have very little rain.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Global warming is considered as an environmental problem because it causes:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Global warming melts ice caps and glaciers and makes the sea expand, so sea level rises, and it also changes rainfall patterns. This leads to **floods** (coastal flooding and heavy rainfall floods) and other hazards such as droughts. Burning fossil fuels and clearing forests are causes of global warming, not effects, and rapid urbanisation is a separate problem.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Many people die in flood plains each year but man still settles there. This is because they have:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Floods deposit layers of silt (alluvium) on the flood plain, so its soils are very **fertile** and give good crop yields, which attracts farmers despite the danger. The other options are weaker: land is not the issue, "much water" is not a reason in itself, and flat land is useful but is not the main reason people accept the risk of flooding.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Global warming can be caused by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trees absorb carbon dioxide. When forests are cut or burnt (**deforestation**), less carbon dioxide is absorbed and the burning releases more of it, so the greenhouse effect is strengthened. Afforestation, reforestation and agroforestry all add trees and therefore help to reduce global warming.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Limestone areas are beautiful landscapes. But they have the main problem of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Limestone is a permeable rock with many joints and it dissolves slowly in rain water, so surface water sinks underground and there are few streams and rivers on the surface. The main problem of limestone areas is therefore the **scarcity of surface water**. Soils are thin, but the question asks for the main problem, which is water.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The destruction of the natural environment has become very rapid today because of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The natural environment is being destroyed quickly mainly because people use natural resources (forests, soils, minerals, fish, water) much faster than nature can renew them, that is **over exploitation of resources**, helped by modern machines and a growing demand. Overgrazing and river pollution are only particular cases, while the option about population does not state a cause directly.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The biotic components of the ecosystem include ONLY:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The biotic (living) components of an ecosystem are the organisms: plants, animals, insects, bacteria and fungi. Air, water, sunlight and rocks are abiotic (non-living) components. Only option A lists living things only.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The rainforest vegetation in Cameroon grows under the influence of the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The tropical rainforest of southern Cameroon grows where the climate is hot and wet all year round: this is the **equatorial climate**, with high temperatures, heavy rainfall and a short dry period. The Sahel and Sudan climates in the north are drier and bear savanna or steppe vegetation, and the mountain climate gives mountain vegetation.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An adaptation of plants in the temperate evergreen forest is that trees:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The temperate evergreen (coniferous) forest is found in cold, snowy areas. Its trees have **narrow, needle-shaped leaves** with a waxy coat, which reduce water loss and let snow slide off, and they keep these leaves all year. Growing very tall and being of many species are features of the equatorial rainforest, while a coniferous forest is dominated by a few species.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Igneous and sedimentary rocks are changed to metamorphic rocks by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Metamorphic rocks form when existing igneous or sedimentary rocks are changed, without melting, by **intense heat and pressure** (for example limestone becomes marble and shale becomes slate). Cooling and solidification of magma forms igneous rocks, and dead plants and animals contribute to organic sedimentary rocks.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The weathering type and process dominant in the Arctic and cold temperate regions is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In cold regions water in the cracks of rocks freezes at night, expands and widens the cracks, then thaws and the process repeats until the rock breaks. This is **physical weathering by frost action** (freeze-thaw). Chemical weathering needs warmth and moisture, biological weathering needs plants, and mechanical weathering by temperature change (insolation) is typical of hot deserts.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The idea from the theory of plate tectonics that talks about the shapes and sizes of continents is called the :

*Options as printed:* A) Kinetic Concept.   B) Geometric Concept.   C) Drifting Concept.   D) Balancing Concept.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The wording of this question is not precise. Wegener's continental drift idea, which led to plate tectonics, started from the observation that the **shapes** of the continents fit together like a jigsaw (for example the east coast of South America and the west coast of Africa). The idea that rests on the shapes and sizes of the continents is the **geometric** concept, so it is the best match to the words used in the question. The drifting concept is about the movement of the continents, the kinetic concept is about motion, and the balancing concept refers to the balance (isostasy) of the earth's crust. Because the four printed names do not clearly match one standard textbook term, this question is treated as open.

**Intended answer: B (Geometric Concept).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Volcanicity produces both intrusive and extrusive features. Select a group that has only intrusive features:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Intrusive features form when magma cools and hardens **below** the surface: batholith, lopolith, sill, dyke and laccolith (printed here as "Lacolith"). Extrusive features form at the surface: crater, caldera, lava flows and cones, with hot springs as a related surface feature. Option A (batholith and lopolith) has two intrusive features. Options B and C each contain an extrusive feature (crater, caldera), and option D contains hot springs, which appear at the surface.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The MOST RECENT measure of the levels of development of countries in the world today is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **Human Development Index (HDI)**, published by the United Nations Development Programme, is the most recent of these measures. It combines life expectancy (health), education and income, so it gives a fuller picture than per capita income, industrial development or energy consumption used alone.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two methods to conserve and manage the world's forest are by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Forests are conserved by planting trees (**afforestation**, and also reforestation) and by cutting only mature trees and leaving the others to grow (**selective cutting**). Option A contains deforestation, which destroys forests, option C is simply the use of forests, and option D limits reforestation, which harms forests.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Supply of timber and forest products.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are methods of mineral extraction from the ground. Which method is best suited for minerals deep below the surface?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Minerals lying deep below the surface are reached by **shaft mining**: a vertical shaft is sunk and horizontal tunnels lead to the ore. Open cast mining is used for minerals near the surface, adit mining uses a horizontal tunnel into a hillside, and submarine mining takes minerals from under the sea.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most widely used source of energy in the World today is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Among the four sources listed, **coal** supplies by far the most energy to the world (oil, which is not offered here, is larger still). Hydro-electric power, biomass and solar energy each supply a much smaller share. Biomass (firewood) is important in poor countries, but at world level coal is ahead.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the list below and select the combination that gives only a set of forest conservation methods?.

(i) Recycling (ii) Selective cutting (iii) Terracing (iv) Granting of lumbering permits (v) Use of substitutes (vi) Education on environmental protection

*Options as printed:* A) i, ii and iv   B) ii, iii and iv   C) iv, v and vi   D) ii, iv and vi
questions.corrige_markdown:
Terracing is a method of soil conservation on slopes, so any option with (iii) is wrong (option B). The core forest conservation methods in the list are selective cutting (ii), granting permits that control lumbering (iv) and education on environmental protection (vi), which is option D. However, recycling (i) of paper and use of substitutes (v) for timber also save trees, so options A and C can be defended as well. The question therefore has more than one acceptable answer and is treated as open.

**Intended answer: D (ii, iv and vi).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the list from below that gives ONLY the characteristics of extensive commercial agriculture.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Extensive commercial agriculture (for example wheat farming on the prairies or large-scale ranching) uses very large farms, few workers and machines. The yield from each hectare or acre is **low** because inputs per unit of land are small, but the yield per worker (per man) is **high**, and the total output is high. Only option A gives the right pair.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Low yield per acre; High yield per man
High yield per acre, High yield per man
Low yield per acre, low total out put
High yield per acre, high total out put

questions.enonce_markdown: Agriculture in the Lowly Industrialised Countries is less productive than that in the Advanced Industrialised Countries of the world because they:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Farmers in the less industrialised countries have **limited capital**, so they cannot buy tractors, improved seeds, fertilisers or irrigation, and their output per hectare and per worker stays low. They do use some machines and fertilisers (so A and B are too strong), and harsh climate is not true for all of them.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The major problem caused by agriculture to the environment is the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Farmers clear forests to make fields and plantations. This **deforestation** exposes the soil to erosion, destroys habitats and reduces the number of species, and it adds carbon dioxide to the air. Reforestation is a remedy, not a problem, and the overproduction of waste or of products are not the major environmental damage.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One assumption of the Weber's theory of industrial location is that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Weber's least-cost theory assumes a uniform plain with **only one mode of transport**, so that transport cost depends only on the weight of the goods and the distance travelled. It also assumes perfect competition, with a market that is not controlled by the government and no monopoly, and it does not assume that raw materials are free (some are found everywhere but still have a cost).

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Only one mode of transport exist.

questions.enonce_markdown: When an industry uses inputs that are light but the products from the industry are heavier, it should be located near the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An industry whose finished product is heavier than its raw materials (a weight-gaining industry, for example bottling drinks, where water is added) should be near the **market**, because moving the heavy product over a long distance would cost more than moving the light inputs. A weight-losing industry would be located near the raw materials instead.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cameroon's cultural wealth for tourism can be seen in her:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cultural wealth means the traditions and heritage made by people, such as the **chiefs' palaces** (for example in the Grassfields) and **annual festivals and dances**. Waterfalls, lakes, forests and wildlife reserves are natural attractions, and roads and hotels are tourist facilities.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The reason why Europe and North America benefit more from global trade is that they have better:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **terms of trade** compare the prices a country gets for its exports with the prices it pays for its imports. Europe and North America export manufactured goods and services, whose prices are high and stable, and import raw materials, whose prices are low and unstable, so they gain more from each unit traded. This is the standard explanation of why developed countries benefit more from world trade.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Air transport is preferred over long distances because it is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Aircraft cover long distances in a short time, are comfortable for passengers and can carry perishable goods (fresh flowers, fruits, fish) before they spoil. Option B is wrong because air transport is not flexible and cannot carry bulky goods, option C is wrong because bad weather can stop flights, and option D is wrong because air transport needs airports and is expensive.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Fast, comfortable and transports perishable goods.
Comfortable, flexible and carries a wide range of goods.
Not affected by weather, knows no traffic congestion and clean.
Fast, accessible to remote areas and cheap.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following processes cause a change in population EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Population changes through births, deaths and migration. The **growth rate** is not a process that causes change: it is the result, a measure of how fast the population changes (natural change plus net migration).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Due to droughts in North Cameroon, farmers abandon the area to the Southern parts. The type of migration involved in this movement is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The farmers move from one region of Cameroon (the North) to other regions (the South) inside the same country: this is **inter-regional (internal) migration**. It is not international because no border is crossed, and the question does not say that they move from villages to towns, or from towns to villages.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The largest unit of a rural settlement is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rural settlements range from the farmstead (a single farm), to the hamlet (a few houses), to the **village**, which is the largest rural unit. A town is an urban settlement.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: On an urban landscape, the settlement unit that will be fewest in number is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In an urban hierarchy the higher the rank of a settlement, the fewer of them there are. A **megalopolis** (a huge urban region formed when several conurbations join) is the largest unit, so there are the fewest. There are many towns, fewer cities, still fewer conurbations.

**Answer: D.**
themes: urban hierarchy and central place theory

questions.enonce_markdown: The creation of green belts in cities is out to solve the problem of :
questions.corrige_markdown:
A green belt is a ring of open land (farmland, forest, parks) around a city where building is controlled. Its main purpose is to stop the city from spreading outwards without control, that is **urban sprawl**, and to protect the countryside.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Shortage of water in the city.
High crime wave in the city.

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the greatest problems encountered when constructing a Multi-purpose River Development Project is
questions.corrige_markdown:
Building the dam of a multi-purpose river project creates a large reservoir that floods the valley, so villages and farmland are lost and **many people must be displaced** and resettled. The other problems are smaller or less certain.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Influx of unemployed to the site

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Adamawa Highlands are very important to Cameroon because it:

*Options as printed:* A) Has many cattle.   B) Is the main watershed.   C) Grows both cereals and tubers.   D) Has many ethnic groups.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Adamawa Highlands (the Adamawa plateau) form the main watershed of Cameroon: rivers flow away from them to the Atlantic, to the Benue and to Lake Chad, so they are the water tower of the country. They are also a major cattle-rearing area, so option A is also true. Because two options can be defended, the question is treated as open. The other two options are not what makes the highlands important to the whole country.

**Intended answer: B (Is the main watershed).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: An argument in favour of the further exploration of oil in Cameroon is that it:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Crude oil is one of Cameroon's main exports, so it brings foreign exchange and government revenue and **contributes to the GDP**. Oil exploration does not protect the environment (it can pollute), the oil industry is capital-intensive and gives work to relatively few people, and Cameroon has one main refinery, so having many refineries is not an argument.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The development of manufacturing industries has been very rapid in the coastal industrial region because of:

*Options as printed:* A) Abundant raw materials.   B) Favourable climate.   C) Political Stability.   D) Government Policy.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The coastal industrial region (Douala, Limbe and Edea) is close to plantations and forests that supply raw materials and has a port that allows imported materials to arrive, so **abundant raw materials** is the factor most often given. The other factors (climate, political stability and government policy) apply to the whole country and do not explain why industry grew faster on the coast, although government policy also helped. Because the answer depends on the textbook used, the question is treated as open.

**Intended answer: A (Abundant raw materials).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The two largest towns in Cameroon are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Douala** (the economic capital and main seaport) and **Yaounde** (the political capital) are by far the two largest cities in Cameroon. Limbe and Bamenda are much smaller.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: There are few roads over the southern low plateau of Cameroon because it has:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The southern plateau is covered by thick equatorial forest crossed by **many rivers** and swamps. Roads are costly to build there, because many bridges are needed and the wet soils and forest are difficult to clear. A dense population or large mineral deposits would call for more roads, and having many airports does not explain a lack of roads.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Government measure to improve agriculture in Cameroon is through the creation of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
To improve agriculture the government creates **research institutes** (such as the Institute of Agricultural Research for Development, IRAD) that develop better seeds, plants and farming methods and advise farmers. More industries, more ministries and more HEP dams do not directly improve farming.

**Answer: B.**
